LESSON: CITIZENSHIP IN KENYA

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Systems
Topic 4.3: Citizenship in Kenya

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Citizenship in Kenya. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we promote responsible citizenship?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. state how one becomes a citizen in Kenya
2. explain requirements for dual citizenship in Kenya
3. demonstrate good citizenship for personal and social well-being
4. appreciate being a good citizen in the community
5. describe the three arms of the National Government in Kenya
6. identify national symbols in Kenya
7. explain factors which promote national unity in Kenya
8. identify basic human rights in Kenya

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CITIZENSHIP IN KENYA
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Citizenship in Kenya helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: CITIZENSHIP IN KENYA
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: State how one becomes a citizen in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to state how one becomes a citizen in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: state how one becomes a citizen in Kenya.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Citizenship in Kenya” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can state how one becomes a citizen in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain requirements for dual citizenship in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to explain requirements for dual citizenship in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain requirements for dual citizenship in Kenya.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Citizenship in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain requirements for dual citizenship in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Demonstrate good citizenship for personal and social well-being

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate good citizenship for personal and social well-being. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate good citizenship for personal and social well-being.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate good citizenship for personal and social well-being. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate being a good citizen in the community

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate being a good citizen in the community. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate being a good citizen in the community.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Citizenship in Kenya” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate being a good citizen in the community. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 5: Describe the three arms of the National Government in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the three arms of the National Government in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the three arms of the National Government in Kenya.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Citizenship in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the three arms of the National Government in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 6: Identify national symbols in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to identify national symbols in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify national symbols in Kenya.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify national symbols in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Citizenship in Kenya is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Citizenship in Kenya” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: state how one becomes a citizen in Kenya)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Citizenship in Kenya. (skill: explain requirements for dual citizenship in Kenya)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: demonstrate good citizenship for personal and social well-being)

Example 4: Connect “Citizenship in Kenya” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: appreciate being a good citizen in the community)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Citizenship in Kenya to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: state how one becomes a citizen in Kenya.
3. Practise this skill: explain requirements for dual citizenship in Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: demonstrate good citizenship for personal and social well-being.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Citizenship in Kenya from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Citizenship in Kenya: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Citizenship in Kenya?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we promote responsible citizenship?
2. How does the government work?
3. which promote national unity in Kenya, How can we promote national unity in our country?
4. Why is it important to respect human rights?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Citizenship in Kenya means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: state how one becomes a citizen in Kenya.
5. Be able to: explain requirements for dual citizenship in Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
